rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and thin zona, but the image is low-contrast/partly collapsed and the response infers features like a focal opening/collapse and detailed ICM/TE quality that are not clearly discernible from the image alone.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, BMI, semen parameters, lining, and lack of prior IVF history with embryo morphology and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent overall, linking morphology and patient factors to prognosis; only minor issue is some overinterpretation of image details relative to confidence.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with Gardner grading use, single embryo transfer in a very young patient, and cautious stance on PGT-A; a few suggestions are more discretionary than guideline-driven.
Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, and targeted evaluation if unsuccessful, though some advice remains somewhat general.
